heading: A Vernon & SilverStar Weekend
title: A Vernon & SilverStar Weekend | Okanagan Roam
description: Two days in Vernon and up at SilverStar: Kalamalka Lake, the Rail Trail, Coldstream and dinner downtown, then skiing, tubing or summer trails on the mountain.
intro: This weekend splits in two. Day 1 stays low, around Vernon and Coldstream: the colours of Kalamalka Lake, a walk or ride on the Rail Trail, and a good dinner in town. Day 2 climbs about 22 km up Silver Star Road to SilverStar for skiing, tubing and snowshoeing in winter or bike and hiking trails in summer. Then you drive back down to Vernon for dinner.

It works in any season, but the mountain changes the most. Winter-only places are marked "(winter, seasonal)", summer-only ones "(summer)". Many patios and some mountain spots cut hours or close between seasons, so check each listing's hours before you set out. If you'd like a plan built around your own dates, our {page:/trip|trip planner} can make one.

sections.heading: Day 1 morning: coffee and Kalamalka Lake
sections.lead: Start downtown, then head south a few minutes to the lake.

items.name: Ratio Coffee & Pastry
items.text: coffee roasted in house, served in a converted rail station with a vintage feel. If you're here on a Tuesday, that's the day the eclairs are baked fresh.

items.name: Kalamalka Lake Lookout
items.text: the classic drive-up view on the old Highway 97, where the "lake of many colours" shifts from turquoise to jade to deep blue. It's a free, wheelchair-accessible rest area with picnic tables facing the water.

items.name: Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park Trails & Rattlesnake Point
items.text: short grassland and forest trails above the lake. The Crest and Juniper trails lead to the viewing platform at Rattlesnake Point. Watch for rattlesnakes, and note that bikes aren't allowed on these trails.

sections.heading: Day 1 afternoon: the Rail Trail and Coldstream
sections.lead: Stay on the Kalamalka side, then finish back in downtown Vernon.

items.name: Okanagan Rail Trail
items.text: a flat, compact gravel trail on the old CN rail bed that hugs the shore of Kalamalka Lake and passes under a historic trestle. Trailhead parking is on Westkal Road in Coldstream and at Kekuli Bay Provincial Park. Dogs must be on leash.

items.name: Rail Trail Café & Market
items.text: sits right beside the trail and is a favourite reward stop for cyclists and hikers. Plan your walk or ride to end here and take a seat on the patio.

items.name: Kal Beach
items.text: swimming and beach volleyball in summer (summer), or a walk out along the Rotary Pier over the water. Dogs aren't on the District's list of parks where they're allowed.

items.name: Kin+Pod Chocolate, Ice Cream, and Coffee
items.text: chocolate, ice cream and coffee all made in house. The owner is happy to let you sample before you choose.

sections.heading: Day 1 evening: dinner in Vernon
sections.lead: Pick one. For more ideas, see our {page:/guides/best-restaurants-vernon|best restaurants in Vernon guide}.

items.name: Cambium Cider Co.
items.text: an orchard cidery with a real restaurant, so a cider stop can turn into dinner. Order beyond a flight, because the kitchen is worth exploring. Go early, as it closes earlier on some nights.

items.name: Intermezzo Restaurant and Wine Cellar
items.text: elegant Italian with a wine cellar, and careful with dietary needs, right down to a gluten-free French onion soup. Live Spanish guitar plays on select nights.

items.name: Suda Restaurant
items.text: widely called the best Korean restaurant in the valley. Order the traditional spicy pork dish and the seafood pancake.

sections.heading: Day 2 morning: up to SilverStar
sections.lead: Drive up Silver Star Road from Vernon. In winter, carry chains or winter tires and check road conditions before you go.

items.name: Bugaboos Bakery Cafe
items.text: the only bakery-cafe in SilverStar Village, with serious plant-based baking such as vegan soy mochas and a vegan banana lava cake. Take in the mountain view with your pastry.

items.name: SilverStar Mountain Resort
items.text: in winter, 133 runs served by ten lifts, and one My1Pass ticket covers downhill, cross-country, snowshoeing, fat biking, skating and tubing. The alpine season runs November 27, 2026 to April 4, 2027. In summer the slopes become the SilverStar Bike Park, and hikers get a free trail day ticket at the Ticket Office for 16 km of trails, including the Ridge Walk from the top of the gondola. Our {page:/guides/ski-season-big-white-silverstar|ski season guide} has more.

items.name: Sovereign Lake Nordic Centre
items.text: Canada's largest cross-country ski and snowshoe club, 2 km west of the resort. It grooms about 58 km for classic and skate skiing, with rentals and lessons at the lodge. More in our {page:/guides/okanagan-nordic-snowshoe|nordic and snowshoe guide}.
items.where: Silver Star Provincial Park, winter, seasonal

items.name: Sovereign Lake Mountain Bike Trails
items.text: in summer the ski trails and singletrack here are a cool, high escape from the valley heat. Expect mostly blue and black, rooty, technical trails, and wet spots early in the season.

sections.heading: Day 2 afternoon: the village, then back down
sections.lead: Lunch in the village, one more winter activity, or a waterfall stop on the drive down.

items.name: The Red Antler
items.text: a village restaurant with both healthy and indulgent options. Order the quinoa avocado power bowl, then the brownie regulars recommend.

items.name: Tube Town SilverStar Tube Park
items.text: big inner tubes, several lanes and a tube lift back to the top. Kids need to be at least three, and it can close without notice in bad weather.

items.name: SilverStar Snowshoe Trails
items.text: 16 km of marked singletrack through the forest, with trailheads at the village and by Brewer's Pond. Rentals are in the village, and leashed dogs are welcome on all of it.

items.name: BX Creek Trail & BX Falls
items.text: on the way down, a short walk from the Tillicum Road parking lot to the falls, with bridges and steep stairs. Spring runoff can make it unsafe, so pick a dry spell. Dogs on leash.

sections.heading: Day 2 evening: dinner back in Vernon

items.name: Masiero Pizzeria Napoletana
items.text: Neapolitan pizza taken toward fine dining, with a strong wine list. The owner tends bar, so let him pick you a cocktail.

items.name: Rustlers Table
items.text: farm-to-table dining on a working farm. Before dinner you can walk past the chickens, cows and sheep.

items.name: Station BBQ Smokehouse
items.text: the owner smokes the brisket and pork ribs personally. Order either one.

items.name: Paradise Camp Snowcat Dinner Tours
items.text: if you'd rather stay up the mountain, a half-hour snowcat ride through the snowy forest to Paradise Camp, then a candlelit multi-course dinner. Select evenings, December to April.

sections.heading: If the weather turns
sections.lead: All in Vernon, and all indoors.

items.name: Okanagan Science Centre
items.text: hands-on exhibits, planetarium shows and live animals in Polson Park. Drop in and pay at the front desk; planetarium shows need pre-registration.

items.name: Vernon Public Art Gallery
items.text: the largest public gallery in the North Okanagan, with changing contemporary shows and admission by donation.

items.name: Planet Bee Honey Farm & Honeymoon Meadery
items.text: watch live bees build comb in viewing hives, then taste honey for free, and honey wine if you're an adult.

items.name: Okanagan Spirits Craft Distillery
items.text: book a guided tour that mixes history with whisky tastings. There are toys on site to keep kids busy.

items.name: The Boarding House Cafe
items.text: a board game cafe with more than 300 games. Order a hot chocolate or a plate of Korean comfort food and settle in.

items.name: Vernon Towne Theatre
items.text: a downtown cinema from 1929 showing new releases, classics and indie films, named Canada's top independent theatre in 2023.

sections.heading: Between seasons and where to stay

items.tip: in late fall and spring, SilverStar sits between its summer and winter seasons and many village spots close. Check each listing first. If the mountain is quiet, spend Day 2 on BX Falls and the Kalamalka trails instead, and save the hill for another trip.
pick a base in Vernon to be close to dinner both nights, or stay up in SilverStar Village in winter if skiing is the main event. Either way, the drive between them is short.
